title: Redwood Console - tracing & request logs debugging walkthrough
topics: RBAC and audit logs for security team
summary: AE/SE walkthrough of Redwood Console focusing on tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Customer had questions about PII redaction, retention, SOC2/KMS, and sampling. Agreed next steps: send security pack, run a 1-week trial with request log retention demo, and schedule a focused latency/throughput benchmark with their inference patterns.
next_steps: Alex to send security questionnaire and SOC2 summary (by 2028-04-17)
Priya to share a short walkthrough video of request-log filters (by 2028-04-18)
Customer to provide sample failing request-id list for root-cause reproduction (by 2028-04-20)
Schedule benchmark pilot for week of 2028-04-24
action_items: Priya: Upload walkthrough clip and sample dashboards (due 2028-04-18)
Olivia: Share 5 failing request-ids and the approximate times (due 2028-04-20)
Maya: Set up trial tenant with 7-day request-logs retention (due 2028-04-19)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-04-15 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex (AE), Priya (SE), Maya (CSM) - Redwood; Jordan (Eng Lead), Samir (CTO), Hannah (Sec Ops), Olivia (SRE) - Acme Health

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we know Acme has been looking at improving debugging flows for production... I'm Alex from Redwood, with Priya who'll do most of the console demo, and Maya if there are any questions on onboarding.
[00:14] Jordan: hey thanks Alex, hi Priya. yeah we're mainly focused on tracing and making it easier for our SREs to triage model failures and e.g. timeouts or bad outputs. we've had some weird 5xxs hitting our callers.
[00:28] Priya: great, that's exactly what we'll walk through - tracing, error analysis, request logs, how you can go from an alert to a root cause quickly. quick caveat: demo uses sanitized data, not real PII.
[00:40] Samir: quick security question up front - retention and encryption: can we get request logs into our S3? and is KMS supported?
[00:49] Priya: yes, good question. Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we have an encrypted-at-rest model and can push logs to your VPC/S3 in Private deployments. I'll show audit logs and the retention controls in the console.
[01:05] Hannah: and SOC2?
[01:07] Alex: we are SOC2 Type II; I'll share the pack after the call.

[01:15] Priya: ok jumping into the console - homepage -> Observability -> Traces. here you can see a list of recent traces, basic filters by model, route, status. note timestamps may show timezone as UTC in the top-right.
[01:30] Speaker 1: (inaudible) it shows something like "K V cache"?
[01:33] Priya: yeah it's "KV cache" - sometimes transcript says "K-V cash" in Fireflies, but the console label is KV cache and you'll see cache hits in the trace waterfall.
[01:42] [02:05] Priya: clicking a trace - the view shows span breakdown, timestamps per span (token generation, kernel exec, network), and any error messages. you can jump to the request log for that request-id directly.
[02:20] Olivia: can we search by request-id? when an alert hits, our pager has a request-id.
[02:25] Priya: absolutely - top-left search box accepts request-id, user-id, model name, or custom tags. I'll demo a filter by request-id now.
[03:00] Priya: filtering to a failing request, you can see the error field - in this example there's a transient socket timeout from our worker. you'll also see downstream retry attempts and the fallback policy noted (we tried open-quant model fallback).
[03:22] Jordan: I see "fallback to 2-bit quant" - that's interesting, do fallbacks change output semantics?
[03:28] Diego: (jumping in) they can, yes - fallbacks are to compatible model variants; we attach a variant tag so you can search for requests served by that variant and compare quality/regressions.
[03:40] [04:10] Priya: error analysis tab aggregates errors by type, route, and model. you can click an error group to see the list of sample requests, an example prompt/response (sanitized), and a histogram of when the errors spiked.
[04:28] Hannah: are responses redacted by default? we can't have PII show up in the console.
[04:32] Priya: yes by default in hosted we redact obvious PII in UI. in Private/Dedicated you can configure whether full payloads are stored; we can also ship redaction hooks to run before logs land in S3. that's in the security pack.
[04:50] [06:00] Priya: next, request logs - this is the raw log stream. you can set retention (7/30/90 days), export to S3, or stream to your SIEM. use filters to narrow by latency, status, or token count. notice the "reproduce" button next to a request - that creates a replay payload you can send to a test endpoint.
[06:20] Jordan: replay would be super useful. does it include the same model variant and KV cache context?
[06:28] Priya: we replay with the same model hash and variant; KV cache isn't replicated across replays by default but we surface the cache key and prefix so you can recreate context or run a synthetic warmup.
[06:42] [07:10] Olivia: about sampling - we get a lot of low-risk traffic. can we sample only errors or high-latency requests?
[07:16] Priya: yes, sampling policies are configurable per-route. default is: retain all errors and a configurable percentage of successes. you can also set token thresholds so long responses get saved.
[07:30] Samir: what about RBAC - can we restrict who sees prompt/response content?
[07:36] Alex: RBAC is per-role in the Console; Sec Ops can get audit-only view. we'll show audit logs next.
[07:45] [08:00] Priya: switching to Audit -> Logs. this contains admin actions, API key rotations, and who accessed traces or request logs. you can export or query by actor.
[08:12] Hannah: do audit logs show the requester IPs?
[08:15] Priya: yes for hosted, it includes region and actor; for Private you get the raw network metadata in your VPC flow logs if you choose to enable them.
[08:30] [09:00] Priya: quick demo of an end-to-end debug flow: alert comes in from Sentry (we have a webhook integration), it links to a trace, you click into an error group, open a sample request, use "reproduce" to hit a sandbox endpoint, and compare outputs across model variants using the A/B diff heatmap.
[09:22] Jordan: how do we do bulk comparisons? like compare output quality across a week?
[09:26] Priya: Optimize has evaluation sets; you can run a batch eval and link regressions back to traces. we'll connect you with the Optimize team for the benchmark pilot.
[09:40] [10:15] Speaker 1: (mumbling) latency numbers show kernel switch times...
[10:20] Priya: yeah you'll see kernel-level timing in the trace spans - compilation, matmul, attention. it's helpful for SREs and infra teams to identify whether latency is compute-bound or I/O-bound.
[10:40] [12:00] Priya: now a quick note on request logs retention and cost: storing full request/response payloads increases storage costs; many customers store metadata and only keep payloads for errors. Redwood's Optimize recommendations can suggest a retention policy per-route based on error rate/cost tradeoffs.
[12:20] Olivia: can we auto-delete after X days and keep hashed pointers?
[12:24] Priya: yes we provide hashed pointers and you can enable auto-purge policies.
[12:35] [14:00] Jordan: on deployments - we're leaning private due to HIPAA concerns; curious about the deployment effort and whether we can have a subset of logs forwarded to our SIEM while the rest are inside Redwood.
[14:12] Alex: for Private you get a customer-controlled control plane, you can choose which sinks to enable. we usually do a lift-and-ship where Redwood sets up the tenant, and we handover ops playbook. Diego can detail the cutover.
[14:28] Diego: typical on-prem timeline is 4-6 weeks for basic set up, longer if you want an air-gapped install. we also support VPC peering and direct S3 writes.
[14:44] [16:00] Priya: back to the trace UI - here's a case study: error spike correlated with a degraded quantization variant. we clicked into the error group, traced it to a new rollout, rolled back the canary from the console, and then scheduled a re-eval.
[16:20] Samir: rollback from console - is that immediate and safe?
[16:24] Priya: yes rollbacks are immediate for routing policies; we include canary config and a preview of traffic percentage. there's also automatic fallback to a stable variant if latency SLOs are violated.
[16:40] [18:00] Jordan: how are request-ids generated? we want to correlate our logs with yours.
[18:04] Priya: each request has a UUID request-id and we also support customer-token to tie back to your user ids. you can ingest that into alerts.
[18:30] [20:00] Priya: small demo: search for request-id, click to open trace, click "open in logs", click reproduce -> choose sandbox -> run. reproduction shows same model hash and attached tags.
[20:30] Olivia: if reproduce fails, can we capture differences?
[20:34] Priya: we capture execution environment diffs: model hash, config, and if KV cache would have influenced output we show the cache key and a note that cache wasn't restored.
[20:50] [22:00] Jordan: about exporting logs, can we stream to Splunk?
[22:05] Priya: yes we have integrations: Splunk, Datadog, your S3 bucket. streaming is via a secure connector.
[22:30] [24:00] Hannah: ok one more - compliance. If we ask for HIPAA BAA, is that available?
[24:06] Alex: we have a HIPAA-ready offering for Private deployments and we sign BAAs for those. Hosted is not HIPAA unless configured as Private.
[24:22] Samir: good to know.
[24:30] [26:00] Priya: wrapping up, a quick look at the error-analysis drill-down - you can add tags, assign to an owner, and open a ticket in Jira directly from the sample.
[26:20] Jordan: perfect - our SREs will love the reproduce button.
[26:30] [28:00] Alex: ok next steps: I'll send SOC2 and security docs, Priya will share the short clip and a sample dashboard, Maya will spin up a 7-day trial tenant so you can try the replay and retention settings.
[28:50] Olivia: we'll also pull 5 failing request-ids and send them.
[29:00] Priya: any other blockers for starting a pilot?
[29:05] Samir: timeline and cost. can you share a pilot pricing model?
[29:10] Alex: yes we'll include pilot pricing and a dedicated SE hours estimate.
[29:18] [31:00] Jordan: small nit - our devs sometimes call KV cache "K-V cache" - so you'll see noisy search terms.
[31:10] Priya: totally fine, the search tolerates fuzzy matches.
[31:30] [35:00] (brief cross chatter as Alex and Priya coordinate follow-ups)
[35:20] Maya: I'll add the meeting notes to the trial tenant and invite Olivia as admin for the trial.
[35:28] Olivia: thanks, appreciated.
[36:00] [40:00] (customers asking about edge cases: very long tokens, billing impact; Priya explains token capping and Optimize's recommendations)
[41:10] Jordan: all good, thanks. last question: will you run a small benchmark with our prompts?
[41:20] Priya: yes, we'll arrange a benchmark - please share a 100-request sample and we'll run throughput/latency and quality comparisons across two model variants.
[41:35] Alex: noted in next steps.
[41:40] [45:00] (closing remarks, Alex thanks everyone)
[45:10] Alex: thanks all - we'll follow up with the security pack and scheduling.
[45:20] Jordan: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
